claims.claim: Program visibility is not contracted volume: Mobileye states OEM sourcing gives two-to-three-year model visibility but OEMs have no contractual commitment to purchase particular volumes and timing/volumes can change.
claims.riskUse: Treat pipeline/design-win figures as conditional conversion evidence, not guaranteed revenue.

claims.claim: Mobileye depends materially on external semiconductor and ECU manufacturing relationships; STMicroelectronics co-developed EyeQ generations, while TSMC is being added for redundancy and future components.
claims.riskUse: Supplier concentration is an observed dependency, while the TSMC qualification path is an explicit resilience improvement rather than a reason to manufacture bearishness.

claims.claim: The 2026 Mentee acquisition used substantial cash and equity, while Mobileye's repurchase authorization is explicitly intended in part to offset dilution from stock compensation and Mentee shares.
claims.riskUse: Physical-AI expansion has measurable capital-allocation and dilution consequences that Alpha can incorporate without Beta assigning a numeric risk score.

claims.claim: Second-quarter guidance improvement in operating loss and adjusted operating income was primarily attributable to an R&D-law incentive, so operating improvement should be normalized before attributing it wholly to underlying leverage.
claims.riskUse: Separates policy-driven benefit from underlying operating performance and reduces confidence inflation.

claims.claim: Mobileye's planned vertically integrated robotaxi service adds fleet operations, rider services and mobility management to its supplier model, creating execution domains beyond supplying autonomous-driving technology.
claims.riskUse: The expansion can create upside but also introduces operating-capital, service-quality and launch-execution falsifiers.

causalEdges.mechanism: production launch and OEM take-rate convert design wins into shipments
causalEdges.falsifier: program timing, volume or sourcing changes before production

causalEdges.mechanism: additional qualified foundry/manufacturing paths reduce single-partner dependency
causalEdges.falsifier: qualification fails or critical components remain effectively single-sourced

causalEdges.mechanism: shared autonomy/AI assets may extend into new human-mobility and robotics needs
causalEdges.falsifier: domain transfer, unit economics, safety approval or commercialization fail to scale

risks: Pipeline/design-win conversion is conditional rather than contracted volume.
Supplier dependence remains material despite active redundancy work.
Mentee and robotaxi expansion add capital-allocation and execution complexity.
Reported operating improvement requires normalization for the R&D-law incentive.
unknowns: Future OEM program take-rates and timing are not contractually fixed.
Economic returns and steady-state capital intensity of the vertically integrated robotaxi operation remain unproven.
Humanoid commercialization economics remain unproven ahead of targeted 2028 series production.
